editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Topology 5.8 Definitions 5.8.1 and 5.8.6. Irreducible components are maximal irreducible sets, whereas a generic point has a prescribed irreducible closure.

definitions.text: A nonempty topological space is irreducible if it cannot be expressed as the union of two proper closed subsets.
An irreducible component of a topological space X is a maximal irreducible subset of X under inclusion; every such component is closed.
A generic point of an irreducible closed subset Z of a topological space X is a point η∈Z such that the closure of {η} equals Z.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Topology 5.20 Definition 5.20.1: immediate specialization is defined using no intervening point, and a dimension function drops one across these relations.

definitions.text: For distinct points x,y of a topological space, y is an immediate specialization of x if y lies in the closure of {x} and no third point lies between x and y in the specialization relation.
A dimension function on a topological space X is an integer-valued map δ:X→Z that strictly decreases on nontrivial specializations and drops by exactly one for immediate specializations.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Commutative Algebra 10.158 Lemma 10.158.8 and Proposition 10.158.9. Formal smoothness of field extensions is characterized by separability in prime characteristic; characteristic-zero extensions are automatically formally smooth.

definitions.text: A field extension K/k is formally smooth over k when every k-algebra map K→A/I across a square-zero quotient lifts to A. In positive characteristic this is equivalent to separability of K/k; in characteristic zero every field extension satisfies it.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: formal smoothness of a field extension

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Categories 4.27, Definition 4.27.1 and Lemma 4.27.8. The localization functor formally inverts arrows from a multiplicative system through a universal property.

definitions.text: A localization of a category C at a multiplicative system S is a category S^{-1}C with functor Q:C→S^{-1}C making each s∈S invertible and universal among functors from C that invert all s∈S.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: localization of a category

definitions.text: A multiplicative system of arrows in a category contains all identities, is closed under composition, and satisfies both left and right Ore-square completion and the corresponding cancellation axioms.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: multiplicative system of arrows

definitions.text: Polynomials f,g∈k[x] over a field k are relatively prime when the ideal (f,g) they generate is the entire polynomial ring k[x].
Two polynomials f,g over a field k are relatively prime if and only if they have no common zero in an algebraic closure of k.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks Topology 5.3, Lemma 5.3.1. Hausdorffness is disjoint-neighbourhood separation; its equivalent diagonal-closed characterization is retained separately.

definitions.text: A topological space X is Hausdorff if every pair of distinct points has disjoint open neighbourhoods.
A topological space X is Hausdorff exactly when the diagonal {(x,x):x∈X} is a closed subset of X×X with its product topology.

editorial_reason: Checked Stacks 10.39, Definition 10.39.1, which expressly distinguishes flatness from faithful flatness for modules and transfers both conditions to ring maps.

definitions.text: An R-module M is flat when the tensor functor −⊗_R M carries every exact sequence of R-modules to an exact sequence.
An R-module M is faithfully flat if tensoring with M preserves and reflects exactness of arbitrary sequences of R-modules.
A ring homomorphism R→S is flat if S is flat as an R-module via the given homomorphism.
A ring homomorphism R→S is faithfully flat if S is faithfully flat as an R-module under the ring map.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: faithfully flat ring map
